title: Sign in: where the address goes
summary: A board of the card's next step for four addresses typed into DJDL's sign-in and one saved passkey: a verified domain that requires SSO, a verified domain that doesn't, an address with no connection (the email code), an SSO-required domain whose connection is down, and a saved passkey picked for an SSO-required address. Beside them, the routing rule in the order the card applies it.
compare: Routing happens in POST /api/signin/email/start (identifier first): a verified domain of a connection goes to that connection; nothing else on the card names SSO before the address is typed.

Pin 1 (SSO required): the identity chip with Change, the organization's name as a one-line heading at the size of the other steps' headings ('Lakeside University', beside a building tile), one primary 'Continue to Lakeside University' with a plain arrow (a same-tab redirect: 'You come back here'), and no email-code or passkey option at all.
Pin 2 (verified, SSO not required): the same heading and primary, plus 'Email me a code instead' as a secondary. The connection comes first; the code still works.

Pin 3 (no connection for the domain): CodeStep exactly as built today (six cells, 'Both work for 10 minutes', 'Send a new code in 0:42', 'Use a different email'). Passkeys were offered on the first step by the browser.

Pin 4 (SSO required, connection down): a danger callout that says why there's no other way in and what to do, 'Try again' as the primary, 'Use a different email'. A domain without SSO required instead falls back to the email code with no error.

Pin 5 (a saved passkey for an SSO-required address): the person picks a passkey from the browser's suggestion on the first step; the server refuses the assertion because the account's address is at a domain with SSO required, and routes to the connection instead: pin 1's body with one note above the heading, 'Lakeside University requires its own sign-in for example.edu, so your passkey can't be used here.' The passkey isn't deleted.
The DJDL header and the footer are identical on every step; only the body changes, with no page navigation and no modal.
The answer never reveals whether an account exists for the address: an unknown address at a verified domain gets exactly pin 1 or 2, an unknown address elsewhere gets pin 3.
Product connections route only on their own product's card; platform connections (Lakeside University here) route on every product's card and on key.plrs.im itself.
An unverified domain (music.example.edu while its TXT record is missing) never routes: it gets pin 3.
Phone: each card is edge to edge in the real flow; on this board the five cards and the rule stack in one column, rule first.
The rule list uses letters (A–E) in neutral marks, so it never reads as the gold pins 1–5.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the saved-passkey route for an SSO-required address is drawn as pin 5, and the board's headings, arrows and numbering are cleaner.

findings.issue: Missing state: what dana@example.edu sees when she picks her saved passkey on the first step, since an SSO-required domain gets no passkey.
findings.resolution: Pin 5 'Passkey for an SSO-required address': pin 1's body with the note 'Lakeside University requires its own sign-in for example.edu, so your passkey can't be used here.' above the heading. Rule B says such an assertion is refused and routed, and the compare adds the server behavior.

findings.issue: Pins 1 and 2 used a heavy two-line heading; two numbering systems (pins 1–4, rule 1–5); a ↗ icon on a same-tab redirect.
findings.resolution: One-line 'Lakeside University' heading at the other steps' size beside a smaller tile; the rule uses letters A–E in neutral marks; the redirect buttons use a plain → arrow.

findings.issue: Hole under the rail at wide, ragged card heights, a design note shown as UI copy.
findings.resolution: The rule list is first, a compact strip of columns above the cards (clamped to 3 lines per item on phone); cards are 400px on one top edge; page intro cut to 'Only the body changes; the header and footer stay.'; the SIGN-IN.md reference and the rail subtitle removed.

findings.issue: Five identical trust footers cost vertical space.
findings.resolution: The footer text and height are unchanged on all five; cards 2 to 5 draw it quieter (.hosted-foot.echo). Not removed: the sheet is a faithful preview.

findings.issue: Delete the A to E rules panel or move it to the JSON notes; rewrite card copy.
findings.resolution: declined: the panel explains the behaviour and is deliberate; only its position and length change; card copy is canonical from SIGN-IN.md.
